newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura shares down in Tokyo on ex-chief's arrest.
newsitem.headline: Nomura shares down in Tokyo on ex-chief's arrest.

text.p: Shares in Nomura Securities Co Ltd fell in early Tokyo trading after media reports that Tokyo prosecutors had arrested former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki in connection with a scandal involving allegedly illegal payoffs to a racketeer.
As of 0013 GMT, the shares were down 20 yen at 1,420 with turnover of 818,000.

"There is a chance that the shares will buckle and test the low of 1,100 yen achieved after the scandal broke," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "But the arrest was expected and the market should be fairly immune to the news."
Brokers added that the impact of the arrest was likely to be limited to Nomura shares.
Later, Tokyo prosecutors confirmed that they had arrested Sakamaki on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in March 1995.

The scandal -- the second involving Nomura in six years -- has dealt a blow not only to the brokerage's bottom line but also to the already tarnished image of Japan's financial institutions as they prepare to compete in Tokyo's increasingly deregulated markets.

Earlier this month Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, two former Nomura executives and a company official alleging they had illegally compensated a firm run by Koike's younger brother Yoshinori.
Prosecutors arrested the two former Nomura executives and the company official as well as the two Koike brothers.
